text: Show this event, not the app in general: what people do or feel during it (a week of grateful mornings, sharing kindness at Christmas, a fresh start in January), told in one image without words.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Build it from the app's own world: the scenes, backgrounds, illustrations and motifs the project draws (read the look's designSource files and the code that draws them). If the app already has a scene that fits the event, such as a holiday, fireworks or a season, start from it. The art should look like the app on its best day.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Make it this event's alone: find what's particular to it in its own texts (gratitude is warmth between people and small kind moments; a 30-day January streak is a fresh start and a climb). Two events of one app share its world and colors, never the same idea, even with the same badge.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Don't redraw the app's icon or mark as the subject: it's a logo, and Apple asks for none. A motif the mark comes from, like a sun or a horizon, is fine as part of a scene.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Aim for the art Apple features on the Today tab: a finished, full-bleed illustration with one clear subject, depth and light. Never a centered symbol on an empty background, a diagram, a pattern or the app's interface.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Make the concepts different ideas, not three versions of one: different subjects, compositions and viewpoints, such as a wide landscape, a close-up of one object, or a gathering of figures or lights.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: One image is shown in every country the event runs in, so prefer what's true everywhere (warm lights, a night sky, people together) over what fits one hemisphere or culture, like snow in December, unless the event is about it.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Shown about 340 to 640 points wide with rounded corners, in search, on Today and on the product page. Apple darkens the lower 60% with its own fade and writes, from the lower left, the badge, the event's name in bold (up to two lines) and the short description, with the app's icon, name and Get button under them. Put the subject in the upper two thirds, at the center or on the right, big enough to read at 340 points wide: a third of the height or more, and at least 6% inside every edge, since the corners are rounded.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: The top of the event's page, full width on iPhone. Apple fades the lower half and writes the badge, the name and the long description there; the top 8% sits under the status bar and the close button. Put the subject in the upper middle, between about 15% and 55% of the height.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: From 60% of the height down, Atlas checks that the art is dark (mean luminance under 0.6) and quiet (few sharp edges) so Apple's white text reads. Keep it part of the picture: ground, water, hills, haze or soft shadow that continue the scene. Never an empty band of flat color.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Depth: three to six layers from back to front (sky, far forms, middle, near silhouettes). Each nearer layer is darker and sharper, the far ones hazier and closer to the sky's color.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Light: one clear source the whole scene answers to, with a glow around it (radial gradients, feGaussianBlur), rim light on the edges that face it, and its color in reflections and on the ground.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Organic shapes: ridges, hills, clouds, plants and figures as paths with many points and varied curves. Never three-point arcs, perfect ellipses or rounded rectangles standing in for things.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Draw the subject with care, from several overlapping shapes with their own light and shadow: a tree's trunk tapers and its branches fork and thin, a firework is glowing trails with falling sparks rather than spokes with dots, a person has a real silhouette (head, shoulders, coat) or isn't drawn at all.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Ground and water are never one flat fill: they take the light (a warm pool under the subject, reflections broken into ripples), fade with distance and carry soft texture.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Texture: a fine grain over everything (an feTurbulence filter at 3 to 6% opacity, on a layer that doesn't move), so large gradients don't band and the page doesn't look like vector clip art. Gradients have four or more stops.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Detail where the eye goes: dozens of stars or particles of different sizes and brightness, small highlights on the subject. Keep the lower part simpler.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Color: the app's palette, lit. The light warms the colors near it and the shadows cool them, instead of big shapes filled with one flat color.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Size html and body to the canvas with overflow hidden. Draw with inline SVG and CSS: JavaScript doesn't run, and web fonts and images from the web don't load.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: The details image is the same world recomposed for the tall frame, not a crop of the card: more sky above, the subject in the upper middle, and the scene going down into the calm lower part.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkDirection

text: Atlas makes a {loopSeconds}-second loop at {loopFramesPerSecond} fps without sound, 1920 × 1080 for the card and 1080 × 1920 for the details page. Apple takes 5 to 30 seconds at 30 or 60 fps.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The still's rules hold: no words or logos, no borders or gradient overlays (Apple adds its own fade and crop), and the card and the details page alike, moving the same way.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The still stays: Atlas keeps the page's first frame as the image, for where video doesn't play.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: Let one thing move that tells the event, and keep the rest of the picture still or nearly still: lanterns rising one by one for gratitude, light travelling from window to window for Christmas kindness, the sun climbing a little higher each morning for a January streak. Around it, a little life: stars twinkling, snow or sparks drifting, mist, a gentle sway. Motion that only decorates, with nothing of the event in it, isn't worth a video.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: Slow and calm: things take seconds to move, ease in and out and travel a short way. No flashing, strobing or flickering (never more than three flashes a second), no shaking, no cuts.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The camera stays put: no zoom or pan of the whole scene, since Apple crops the card differently in each place. A slight parallax between layers, a few percent of the width at most, is fine.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The first frame is the still and has to work alone: everything already in place at 0 seconds, nothing fading in from an empty scene or entering from outside the frame at the start.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: Seamless: every animation repeats a whole number of times in {loopSeconds} seconds (durations of 1, 2, 2.5, 4, 5, 10 or 20 s, animation-iteration-count: infinite), with its 0% and 100% keyframes the same. Stagger with a negative animation-delay, never a positive one. Something that travels comes back to where it started by the end, or fades out and in again at the same spot.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The lower part stays calm under Apple's text: at most a slow shimmer on water or drifting haze, never a moving subject behind the words.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: The details image moves the same elements at the same rhythm as the card, so opening the card into the event's page feels like one piece.
view: In-App Events › Event artwork studio › EventArtworkMotion

text: Before sending a concept, render its card and its details image with render_event_artwork and motionFrames: true, and look at the frames it returns and at its loop check. It's quick: the video itself is made when you send the concept.

The person asked for some screens of the custom product page “%@” of %@ (app %@) to be captured again, so they show what this page’s audience came for. Work in this order.
1. Read get_page_screenshots with page “%@”: the page, the plan, the default set’s screens (their captures are attached) and `recapture`, with its upload link and the devices and languages it needs.
2. Choose at most %lld screens whose capture should show something else for this audience (the lock turned on, the kind of entries this page is about). Leave the others as they are.
3. Look for the project’s screenshot UI tests first (Grep for XCUIScreen or screenshot in its UI test files): they reach the screens that need taps and set up sample data. Run the ones for your screens with xcodebuild test -only-testing:… -resultBundlePath <path>, with the values they read (a topic, an entry) given after xcodebuild as build settings, NAME=value (their comments or the test scheme’s environment say which; nothing goes in front of xcodebuild), and export the captures with xcrun xcresulttool export attachments. Without such tests, build the app and run it in the Simulator with the app’s launch arguments, then save the screen with xcrun simctl io booted screenshot. Use %@ for iPhone, %@ for iPad, turned the way `recapture` says (its devices’ orientation and pixel size), in each language the set is made in (-testLanguage and -testRegion, or -AppleLanguages and -AppleLocale).
4. Send each PNG with curl -s --data-binary @file.png -H 'Content-Type: image/png' <uploadURL>, the link as is (not in quotes), and name it with report_page_capture: the screen’s number, the language, the device, the upload ID and what it shows now.
Never push and never submit the page, and don’t change the app’s code: the person makes the set in Atlas.
